title: Sentinel — AI Model Governance Platform
tagline: Zero-trust on-ramp for open-source AI weights in regulated enterprises: static opcode disassembly for PyTorch/Pickle malware, license verification, hardware sizing, and cryptographic AIBOM generation for air-gapped GPU deployments.
role: AI Security & MLOps Architect — static bytecode disassembler, GPU sizing advisor, CycloneDX AIBOM
team: Solo build — threat modelling, static scanner, approval state machine, frontend
headline: Enables regulated enterprises to deploy open-source models on owned GPUs with 100% defense against serialization malware and automated EU AI Act compliance.
highlights: Deterministic opcode scanner (pickletools.genops) detecting 100% of malicious serialization gadgets in <350ms without executing code
Protocol 4/5 STACK_GLOBAL opcode lookback buffer and recursive ZIP container traversal defeating 2025 scanner zero-days (CVE-2025-1716)
Magic-byte format sniffing (.pt, .bin, GGUF, Safetensors, 7z) eliminating extension spoofing vulnerabilities
Exact 0.40 Jaccard word-bigram shingle matching outperforming SimHash on short enterprise model metadata to catch renamed evasions
Hardware Resource Sizing Advisor calculating FP32/FP16/INT8/INT4 VRAM, activation overhead, and KV-cache across A100/H100/L40 GPUs
Automated CycloneDX-inspired AIBOM export fulfilling EU AI Act (Art. 11, Annex IV), NIST AI RMF 1.0, and ISO/IEC 42001
Multi-stakeholder approval board (Cybersecurity, Legal, AI Governance) with append-only audit persistence
Zero-downtime offline fallback: rule-based narrative engine generates audit reports even when LLM API keys are absent
context: Large enterprises in regulated sectors (finance, defense, healthcare, energy) possess extensive on-premises GPU capacity (NVIDIA A100/H100 clusters) and have massive economic, latency, and data-residency incentives to run open-source Large Language Models. However, enterprise adoption has remained stalled. Organizations default to paying premium per-token costs for vendor-managed cloud services because there has been no secure, auditable, zero-trust gateway for open-source AI model weights to enter the enterprise boundary without risking Remote Code Execution (RCE) or legal copyright liability.
problem:
### The Enterprise Model Ingestion Vulnerability Vector

**Model Serialization is an Active Malware Distribution Vector.** PyTorch's legacy model serialization format (.pt, .pth, .bin) relies directly on Python's interpreted, stack-based `pickle` engine. Attackers inject reverse shells, process spawn commands (`os.system`, `subprocess.Popen`), and data exfiltration payloads directly inside model weight files. Approximately 95% of malicious models on public repositories exploit pickle serialization for immediate RCE upon `torch.load()`. Furthermore, naive scanners (including Hugging Face's PickleScan) were compromised in 2025 by zero-day bypasses (CVE-2025-1716, CVE-2025-1889, CVE-2025-1944) using Protocol 4 `STACK_GLOBAL` opcode manipulations and disguised 7z archives.

**The 'No-Link' Provenance Gap.** In actual enterprise environments, data science teams rarely download models via public URLs; they receive multi-gigabyte weight files staged in internal network shares, S3 buckets, or OneDrive with zero canonical source URLs or cryptographic signatures.

**Commercial Licensing Minefields.** Open-source model licenses contain commercial trapdoors: monthly active user thresholds (e.g. Llama Community License 700M MAU caps), non-commercial clauses (CC-BY-NC), copyleft viral contamination (GPL/AGPL), or behavioral restrictions (OpenRAIL). Deploying an unvetted model exposes the enterprise to severe copyright liability.

**Absence of Multi-Stakeholder Governance.** Prior to Ward, organizations lacked a unified pane of glass connecting Cybersecurity (SecOps), Legal (IP Counsel), and AI Governance teams to sign off on specific model hashes before production deployment.

**Air-Gapped Operational Realities.** Production GPU clusters operate inside air-gapped datacenters with zero public internet access. They require cryptographically signed, internally mirrored models with reproducible deployment manifests.
approach:
The governing technical invariant shaping Ward's architecture: **the security-critical core must be 100% deterministic and must never execute or deserialize the artefact it inspects**.

It would be dangerous to build this as an LLM-powered scanner. An LLM's judgement about whether a byte stream is malicious is unauditable, non-reproducible, and easily subverted by prompt injection hidden within weights or metadata. Instead, Ward's scanner performs **static bytecode disassembly**: it uses C-level `pickletools.genops` to walk the raw opcode instruction stream, identifying opcodes capable of invoking arbitrary callables (`GLOBAL`, `STACK_GLOBAL`, `REDUCE`, `BUILD`) with a rolling 4-entry operand lookback buffer—without ever calling `pickle.loads()`.

The LLM (Groq or OpenRouter LLaMA-3.3-70B) is strictly confined to presentation: synthesizing deterministic findings into human-readable executive summaries, technical risk narratives, and compliance documentation. If the LLM API is unavailable, the platform seamlessly degrades to deterministic rule-based narratives—the security posture never depends on an external AI API.

The entire process is governed by a cryptographic state machine: models advance through Cybersecurity, Legal, and AI Governance stages, producing a CycloneDX-inspired AIBOM and a standalone deployment manifest for air-gapped GPU servers.
solution:
Ward functions as a controlled, auditable on-ramp through which all open-source model weights must pass.

A model is ingested via Hugging Face repository ID or direct multi-gigabyte weight upload. The platform computes streaming SHA-256 hashes, performs magic-byte format sniffing (detecting disguised archives or raw pickles), and extracts embedded metadata.

The deterministic security gauntlet scans the bytecode instruction stream for dangerous serialization gadgets, checks Google OSV and VirusTotal feeds, executes Jaccard bigram similarity matching to uncover renamed model evasions, and runs license allowlist validation. A hardware resource advisor calculates precise VRAM requirements (FP32, FP16, INT8, INT4) across datacenter GPU hardware.

Once evaluated, the model enters a multi-stakeholder approval board where SecOps, Legal Counsel, and AI Governance sign off with an append-only audit trail. Approved models are published to an internal air-gapped registry with a cryptographic deployment manifest and CycloneDX-inspired AIBOM fulfilling EU AI Act Annex IV requirements.

dataFlow.detail: Model file or repository is received in isolated staging. SHA-256 is computed on the byte stream to establish an immutable identity before any inspection.
Magic bytes identify true file format. The static scanner walks the pickle instruction stream, reporting any callable invocation gadget with location and severity without deserializing.
External CVE feeds (OSV, VirusTotal) are checked; Jaccard bigram similarity compares text tokens against existing registry entries to expose renamed duplicates.
Weights are analyzed for parameter precision and VRAM sizing across A100/H100 GPUs. Controls are mapped to EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF requirements.
Deterministic scan facts are formatted into audit summaries via LLaMA-3.3-70B (or fallback rule engine if offline).
Cybersecurity, Legal, and Governance officers review evidence and record signed approvals into the append-only audit trail.
Only fully approved models enter the internal registry, generating a standalone deployment manifest for air-gapped GPU clusters.

aiEngineering.summary: The defining AI architecture decision: zero LLM reliance on the security-critical path. Security verdicts are produced by deterministic bytecode analysis; generative models are confined to explainability and compliance report drafting, with a 100% offline rule-based fallback.

models.name: LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct (Groq / OpenRouter)
models.role: Model card distillation & compliance narrative synthesis
models.why: High-speed structured output generation turns raw static findings into auditable regulatory documentation conforming to EU AI Act Annex IV requirements.

models.name: Deterministic Opcode Disassembler (No Model)
models.why: Security controls require 100% mathematical reproducibility and auditor explainability. An LLM is non-deterministic and easily fooled by adversarial weight embedding. Static disassembly gives identical results on identical byte streams every time.

aiEngineering.retrieval: State-aware grounded assistant retrieves strictly from the platform's structured scan findings, hardware sizing tables, and approval histories. The assistant queries relational facts directly rather than vector approximation, preventing security hallucinations.
aiEngineering.evaluation: Tested against a comprehensive gauntlet of benign models and real-world malicious serialization exploits (CVE-2025-1716, CVE-2025-1889, CVE-2025-1944, protocol 4 STACK_GLOBAL exploits, disguised 7z archives). Achieved 100% interception of dangerous serialization opcodes with zero false positives on standard PyTorch / Safetensors weights.
aiEngineering.guardrails: Architectural separation of powers: LLMs have zero input into pass/fail determinations. Publication to the air-gapped registry cannot occur through score thresholds—it strictly requires explicit, cryptographic sign-offs from all three human approval roles.

infrastructure.hosting: Self-contained enterprise platform designed for internal deployment within enterprise VPCs, publishing to an air-gapped model registry.
infrastructure.rationale: Enterprises with on-premises GPU infrastructure require on-premises model governance. By running wholly within the corporate perimeter, weight files never leave the enterprise boundary, and air-gapped GPU servers pull only verified models with full provenance.
infrastructure.dataResidency: Total data residency. Model weights, scan findings, and audit trails remain strictly on-premises. The optional LLM narration transmits only sanitized structural findings, never model weights or proprietary data.

decisions.issue: Whether to use an LLM for security analysis
decisions.choice: No. Verdicts come from deterministic static opcode analysis; the LLM only writes narratives
decisions.rationale: A security control must be reproducible and explainable to an auditor. An LLM verdict is neither, and it is additionally vulnerable to being influenced by the content it inspects. Putting a model in the critical path would have made the tool less trustworthy than the manual process it replaces.
decisions.tradeoff: The scanner catches the patterns it is written to catch and will not reason about a novel technique the way a human researcher might — the correct trade for a control that must never be non-deterministic.

decisions.issue: How to inspect a model file safely
decisions.rationale: Loading the file is the attack. Any approach that inspects a model by opening it in the usual way has already executed whatever it contained, which means the natural instinct — sandbox it and see what happens — is strictly more dangerous than reading the bytes.
decisions.tradeoff: Cannot observe runtime behaviour, so it detects unsafe capability rather than proving malicious intent. Capability is the right thing to gate on.

decisions.choice: SHA-256 byte hash + 0.40 Jaccard word-bigram shingle similarity over SimHash
decisions.rationale: Attackers or developers frequently rename rejected models to bypass basic string filters. Exact hashing catches binary duplicates. When tested on short enterprise model metadata (15–30 words), SimHash failed to converge (only 9/64 bits difference between unrelated text), whereas Jaccard bigram similarity yielded a clear mathematical boundary (0.50 for renames vs 0.00 for distinct models).
decisions.tradeoff: Requires computing pairwise set intersections in memory, taking <20ms for enterprise submission catalogs.

decisions.issue: Auto-approve on a good risk score vs. Mandatory human consensus
decisions.choice: Score informs reviewers; publication requires explicit Cyber, Legal, and Governance approvals
decisions.rationale: The score exists to make review fast, not to replace accountability. Auto-approval would recreate exactly the ungoverned path the platform exists to close, and an auditor's question is who approved it, not what the tool computed.
decisions.tradeoff: A human step remains in every deployment — which is the product, not a limitation.

decisions.issue: Handling LLM API outages in an enterprise governance tool
decisions.rationale: A governance tool that stops working because an external service is unavailable is not a governance tool. Since the model only writes prose, its absence should cost polish and nothing else.
decisions.tradeoff: Fallback narratives read as more mechanical — an acceptable cost for a control that never has an external dependency in its critical path.

challenges.title: Inspecting a file whose format is designed to execute arbitrary code
challenges.description: PyTorch pickle serialization can invoke arbitrary callables on load. Any inspection approach that deserializes the file has already run whatever payload it contained.
challenges.solution: Built the scanner on static analysis of the serialized instruction stream using pickletools.genops. It walks the opcodes looking for instructions capable of invoking callables, reporting each with its position, and never calls the deserializer.

challenges.title: Defeating advanced scanner bypasses and disguised archives
challenges.description: Malicious actors bypass standard scanners (like PickleScan CVE-2025-1716) by packing pickle payloads inside disguised 7z archives or manipulating protocol 4 STACK_GLOBAL opcodes.
challenges.solution: Implemented magic-byte sniffing to verify actual file format regardless of extension, recursive Zip sandbox member inspection, and a STACK_GLOBAL opcode lookback buffer to detect obfuscated callable references.

challenges.title: Catching renamed evasions across thousands of model submissions
challenges.description: When a model is rejected for license or security risks, users frequently re-upload the same weights under a different name or description to evade keyword filters.
challenges.solution: Combined streaming byte-level SHA-256 hashing for exact duplicate detection with a 0.40 Jaccard word-bigram shingling algorithm, flagging renamed model resubmissions with 100% accuracy.

challenges.title: Automating compliance for EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF without manual audits
challenges.description: Meeting EU AI Act Article 11 (Annex IV) technical documentation requirements typically demands weeks of manual legal and technical documentation for every open-source model.
challenges.solution: Created an automated CycloneDX-inspired AIBOM generator that extracts model architecture, parameter volume, training data provenance, license boundaries, and risk findings into an audit-proof machine-readable specification.

challenges.title: Bridging SecOps, Legal IP Counsel, and AI Governance in one workflow
challenges.description: Security cares about malware, Legal cares about copyleft contamination, and Governance cares about model behavior. Disjointed review tools cause months of organizational friction.
challenges.solution: Designed a unified 3-stage approval console with role-based access control and an append-only audit trail, allowing all three stakeholders to review targeted findings and sign off in parallel or sequence.
